newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady, shrugs off repo drain.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady, shrugs off repo drain.

text.p: German call money rates were little moved on Wednesday as banks shrugged off a 1.1 billion-mark net drain of funds at the weekly repo allocation.
Call money rates were quoted at 3.00/3.05 percent after the bulk of trades on Tuesday had been at 3.00 percent.
Dealers said the net repo drain had neatly absorbed a slight suplus of liquidity that had been evident at the start of the week.
"We had a little too much liquidity, so the drain is acceptable," one money dealer said.

Effective commercial bank deposits at the the Bundesbank totalled 40.0 billion marks on Tuesday, up from 39.1 billion on Monday, while the monthly average on Tuesday was unchanged at 40.0 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings remained negligible on Tuesday, The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was 3.04533 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.03867 percent on Tuesday.
